content: 1. Beta Blocker Dose: Monitor closely when adjusting beta blocker doses, as interactions with other medications may require careful titration. 2. Atazanavir and Tinidazole: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of tinidazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Atazanavir and Tipranavir: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of tipranavir through CYP3A4 enzyme inhibition. Both drugs also increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use an alternative therapy if possible. 4. Tipranavir and Atazanavir: Tipranavir increases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Atazanavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Atazanavir increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tisotumab vedotin’s active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use an alternative therapy if possible. 6. Atazanavir and Tofacitinib: Atazanavir increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily and monitor closely. 7. Atazanavir and Tolterodine: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 8. Atazanavir and Tolvaptan: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Topiramate and Atazanavir: Topiramate decreases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 10. Atazanavir and Toremifene: Atazanavir increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 11. Atazanavir and Trabectedin: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next trabectedin infusion. Monitor closely. 12. Atazanavir and Tramadol: Atazanavir increases the levels of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Atazanavir and Trazodone: Atazanavir increases trazodone levels through an unspecified mechanism and by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 14. Atazanavir and Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of triamcinolone acetonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 15. Atazanavir and Triazolam: Atazanavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Atazanavir and Trimipramine: Atazanavir increases trimipramine levels through an unspecified mechanism and by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 17. Tucatinib and Atazanavir: Tucatinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling and monitor closely. 18. Ublituximab and Atazanavir: Ublituximab decreases the effects of atazanavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Atazanavir and Ubrogepant: Atazanavir increases ubrogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Atazanavir and Ulipristal: Atazanavir increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 21. Atazanavir and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol Inhaled: Atazanavir increases the levels of umeclidinium bromide and vilanterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Atazanavir and Upadacitinib: Atazanavir increases upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and monitor closely. 23. Atazanavir and Valbenazine: Atazanavir increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and monitor closely. 24. Atazanavir and Vamorolone: Atazanavir increases vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if the patient weighs more than 50 kg. Monitor closely. 25. Atazanavir and Vardenafil: Atazanavir increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the dose to 5 mg per 24 hours and monitor closely. 26. Atazanavir and Velpatasvir: Atazanavir increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 27. Atazanavir and Vemurafenib: Atazanavir increases vemurafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Atazanavir and Venetoclax: Atazanavir increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. Monitor closely. 29. Atazanavir and Verapamil: Atazanavir increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and verapamil increases atazanavir levels through the same mechanism. Use caution, as this combination may increase the risk of AV block. Monitor closely. 30. Atazanavir and Vilazodone: Atazanavir increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 31. Atazanavir and Vinblastine: Atazanavir increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 32. Atazanavir and Vincristine: Atazanavir increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 33. Atazanavir and Vincristine Liposomal: Atazanavir increases vincristine liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 34. Atazanavir and Vinorelbine: Atazanavir increases vinorelbine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 35. Atazanavir and Voclosporin: Atazanavir increases voclosporin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Atazanavir and Vonoprazan: Vonoprazan decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 37. Atazanavir and Vorapaxar: Atazanavir increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 38. Atazanavir and Voriconazole: Atazanavir increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and voriconazole increases atazanavir levels through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Atazanavir and Voxilaprevir: Atazanavir increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Atazanavir and Warfarin: Atazanavir increases warfarin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 41. Atazanavir and Zafirlukast: Zafirlukast increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 42. Atazanavir and Zaleplon: Atazanavir increases zaleplon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 43. Atazanavir and Zanubrutinib: Atazanavir increases zanubrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 44. Atazanavir and Zidovudine: Both atazanavir and zidovudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 45. Atazanavir and Zileuton: Atazanavir increases zileuton levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 46. Atazanavir and Ziprasidone: Atazanavir increases ziprasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 47. Atazanavir and Zolpidem: Atazanavir increases zolpidem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 48. Atazanavir and Zonisamide: Atazanavir increases zonisamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 49. Atazanavir and Zuranolone: Atazanavir increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 50. Adverse Effects and Monitoring: Common adverse effects include increased bilirubin, fever, rash, elevated cholesterol, nausea, increased CPK, cough, diarrhea, neutropenia, jaundice, headache, peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, vomiting, dizziness, myalgia, abdominal pain, and depression. Serious cardiovascular effects include secondor third-degree AV block, left bundle branch block, and QTc prolongation. Hepatic effects include pancreatitis, hepatic function abnormalities, and hepatobiliary disorders such as cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, and cholestasis. Metabolic effects include diabetes mellitus, hyperglycemia, and fat redistribution. Renal effects include chronic kidney disease, nephrolithiasis, and interstitial nephritis. Skin reactions include alopecia, angioedema, maculopapular rash, and pruritus. Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, have been reported. Immune reconstitution syndrome and autoimmune disorders (e.g., Graves’ disease, polymyositis, Guillain-Barré syndrome) may occur. Patients with hepatitis B or C are at increased risk of elevated transaminases or hepatic decompensation. 51. Special Considerations: Avoid proton pump inhibitors in treatment-experienced patients. Discontinue therapy if severe rash or hypersensitivity reactions occur. Monitor ECG in patients with preexisting conduction system disease or when coadministered with drugs that prolong the PR interval. Conduct renal laboratory testing before and during therapy, especially in patients at high risk for renal disease. Consider alternative therapy in patients with progressive kidney disease or confirmed renal abnormalities. Temporary interruption or discontinuation may be necessary for nephrolithiasis or cholelithiasis.
